title: Biotechnological process optimization
text: first want load ChemicalManufacturingProcess data set (originally AppliedPredictiveModeling package) transform data.table. also give process variables shorter names, interactive plots generated alter easier read. Since data contains many NA’s need clean can start analysis. first remove rows >3 NA’s, columns >3 NA’s, remove datapoints extreme outliers, finally remove columns still contain NA’s. want visualize distribution yield. Therefore, first categorize 10 groups depending yield, visualize histogram. also store labels groups later use.  Finally, standardize data remove yield.
code: library(lionfish) library(data.table)  data(ChemicalManufacturingProcess) data <- data.table(ChemicalManufacturingProcess) col_names <- names(data)  mp_cols <- grep("^ManufacturingProcess", col_names, value = TRUE) bm_cols <- grep("^BiologicalMaterial", col_names, value = TRUE)  new_mp_names <- sub("^ManufacturingProcess", "ManPr", mp_cols) new_bm_names <- sub("^BiologicalMaterial", "BioMat", bm_cols)  setnames(data, old = mp_cols, new = new_mp_names) setnames(data, old = bm_cols, new = new_bm_names) data <- data[rowSums(is.na(data))<3] data <- data[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (sum(is.na(x)) <= 3) x else NULL)] data <- data[-c(99,153,154,158,159,160)] data <- data[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (sum(is.na(x)) <= 0) x else NULL)] min_yield <- min(data$Yield, na.rm = TRUE) max_yield <- max(data$Yield, na.rm = TRUE)  intervals <- seq(min_yield, max_yield, length.out = 11) yield_values <- findInterval(data$Yield, intervals, rightmost.closed = TRUE) yield_labels <- paste0("Yield ", head(intervals, -1), "-", tail(intervals, -1)) library(ggplot2) library(viridis) #> Loading required package: viridisLite yield_values_factor <- factor(yield_values, labels = yield_labels)  ggplot(data, aes(x = Yield, fill = yield_values_factor)) +   geom_histogram(binwidth = (max_yield - min_yield) / 30, color = "black") +   scale_fill_viridis(option = "plasma", discrete = TRUE) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Histogram of the process yield",        x = "Yield",        y = "Count",        fill = "Yield Intervals") data <- data[, lapply(.SD, function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))] data_wo_y <- copy(data) data_wo_y[, Yield := NULL]

title: Biotechnological process optimization
text: Now prepared data, can visualize lionfish. Therefore, first initialize python backend init_env(), generate two tour history objects tourr package. tours use linear discriminant analysis projection pursuit index, aims maximize separation 10 different yield groups. One tour history object projects 1D one projects 2D. Next, estimate appropriate initial value half range display. half range acts scaling factor, determining extent data spread graphical interface. instance, initial estimate caused data points appear close together. improve visualization, reduced half range half, resulting effective display data. , plot objects defined. Plot objects named lists specify type display shown display specific additional information. case want display “1d_tour” “2d_tour” give objects previously generated tour histories. Finally, start interactive tour closer look data. First, set “Blend projection threshold” 0.2. setting causes projection axes norm less 0.2 blended , helps reduce clutter plot. Next, set time interval next “Animate” 0.1 seconds. adjustment causes plots move next projection tour objects every 0.1 seconds (note animation speed may slightly slower depending rendering time frame). Noticeable separation yield groups begins occur around frame 10 becomes even pronounced frame 30 onward. successfully identified projections explain differences yield Let’s investigate projections . Projection axes point towards high yield groups large positive influence , whereas projection axes point away negative influence yield. better understand influence, can move mouse cursor arrowheads see original process parameter axis represents. can also change axes dragging dropping arrowhead right mouse button. adjust longest projection axis point towards high yield groups, first observe axis arrow represents manufacturing process 09 (ManPr09). Extending direction high yield groups leads greater separation, dragging opposite direction results worse separation. suggests high values manufacturing process 09 associated higher yields. However, changing axis point opposite direction, notice groups start mix. indicates variable manufacturing process 09 alone sufficient explain yield. , changing direction manufacturing process 09 simply invert data, still see high yield groups aligned manufacturing process 09 axis. can now adjust axes see can identify interactions parameters. instance, elongate axis representing manufacturing process 32, observe positive interaction two variables. confirm influence, can drag axes opposite direction. Unlike changing manufacturing process 32, action somewhat inverts data. indicates two variables together already explain yield quite well. since separation isn’t clear original projection see high yield groups aren’t exactly direction two axes, still need variables fully explain influence yield. Furthermore, can vary process parameters capture interactions potential structural patterns. instance, adjusting axis representing manufacturing process 31, observe outlier low value parameter (data point opposite direction axis) slightly -average yield. Varying manufacturing process 40 results two clearly separated groups. indicates variable two discrete settings. clear indication variable strong influence yield can see high low yield data points groups.
code: set.seed(42) # the development version of tourr is required, otherwise the 1d lda tour # will crash! remotes::install_github("ggobi/tourr") library(tourr)  display_size <- 5 # Adjust to fit your display  init_env()  lda_tour_history_1d <- save_history(data_wo_y,                                     tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(yield_values),d=1))  lda_tour_history_2d <- save_history(data_wo_y,                                      tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(yield_values),d=2))  half_range <- max(sqrt(rowSums(data_wo_y^2))) feature_names <- colnames(data_wo_y)  obj1 <- list(type="1d_tour", obj=lda_tour_history_1d) obj2 <- list(type="2d_tour", obj=lda_tour_history_2d) interactive_tour(data=data_wo_y,                  plot_objects=list(obj1,obj2),                  feature_names=feature_names,                  half_range=half_range/2,                  n_plot_cols=2,                  preselection=yield_values,                  preselection_names=yield_labels,                  display_size=8,                  color_scale="plasma")

text: Now got first overview data, can refine visualization fitting random forest model, predicts yield based process variables, selecting important variables according model. analysis 10 important chosen. can take R output 10 important process parameters according random forest model manufacturing processes 09, 13, 17, 31, 32, 36, biological materials 03, 06, 11 12. next step reduce dataset contain variables visualize data way earlier. can see already separation initial frame, can still achieve good separation yield groups. extreme groups even better separated compared projection process parameters. final frame, observe manufacturing processes 09 32, well biological material 12, positive influence yield, manufacturing processes 17 36 negative influence. may interested enhancing separation groups particularly low high yields. quick method achieve adjusting opacity groups less interested , initializing local tour search projections better separate highlighted groups. final frame, observe separation extreme groups improved slightly. identify interesting frame, can save pressing “Save projections subsets.” allows us continue analysis later. reload saved data, can use GUI pressing “Load projections subsets” selecting appropriate folder, can load programmatically using function load_interactive_tour(). elegant way define three yield bins run another guided tour. can see results even better separation. , can run local tour see can improve separation observe another interesting angle. case still wouldn’t happy projections, run another guided tour - LDA within interface (shown ).
code: set.seed(42) library(randomForest) rf <- randomForest(Yield~.,data) importance_df <- data.frame(rf$importance) importance_df <- as.data.table(rf$importance, keep.rownames = "Feature") sorted_importance <- importance_df[order(-IncNodePurity)] top_10_features <- sorted_importance[1:10, Feature] print(top_10_features) #>  [1] "ManPr32"  "ManPr13"  "BioMat12" "BioMat03" "ManPr09"  "ManPr17"  #>  [7] "BioMat06" "ManPr36"  "ManPr31"  "BioMat11" data_rf_sel <- data[, ..top_10_features]  grand_tour_history_1d <- save_history(data_rf_sel,                                       tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(yield_values),d=1))  lda_tour_history_2d <- save_history(data_rf_sel,                                      tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(yield_values),d=2))  half_range <- max(sqrt(rowSums(data_rf_sel^2))) feature_names <- colnames(data_rf_sel)  obj1 <- list(type="1d_tour", obj=grand_tour_history_1d) obj2 <- list(type="2d_tour", obj=lda_tour_history_2d) interactive_tour(data=data_rf_sel,                  plot_objects=list(obj1,obj2),                  feature_names=feature_names,                  half_range=half_range/2,                  n_plot_cols=2,                  preselection=yield_values,                  preselection_names=yield_labels,                  n_subsets=11,                  display_size=8,                  color_scale = "plasma") intervals <- seq(min_yield, max_yield, length.out = 4) new_yield_labels <- paste0("Yield ", head(intervals, -1), "-", tail(intervals, -1))  new_min_yield <- min(data$Yield, na.rm = TRUE) new_max_yield <- max(data$Yield, na.rm = TRUE)  new_intervals <- seq(new_min_yield, new_max_yield, length.out = 4) new_yield_values <- findInterval(data$Yield, new_intervals, rightmost.closed = TRUE) grand_tour_history_1d <- save_history(data_rf_sel,                                       tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(new_yield_values),d=1))  lda_tour_history_2d <- save_history(data_rf_sel,                                      tour_path = guided_tour(lda_pp(new_yield_values),d=2))  half_range <- max(sqrt(rowSums(data_rf_sel^2))) feature_names <- colnames(data_rf_sel)  obj1 <- list(type="1d_tour", obj=grand_tour_history_1d) obj2 <- list(type="2d_tour", obj=lda_tour_history_2d) interactive_tour(data=data_rf_sel,                  plot_objects=list(obj1,obj2),                  feature_names=feature_names,                  half_range=half_range/2,                  n_plot_cols=2,                  preselection=new_yield_values,                  preselection_names=new_yield_labels,                  n_subsets=3,                  display_size=8,                  color_scale = "plasma")
